message.content: The probes ran cleanly and decisively contradict all three claims. Key insight: because seq labels are nondecreasing, a token whose label differs from the chunk's first-token label is exactly a post-boundary token, so `_combine`'s zeroing is correct even mid-chunk; and `_pass_states`' last-token representative label catches any in-chunk boundary. I'll finalize all three as rebutted.

message.reasoning_content:
All three probes show no errors — surprising given the source analysis. Wait — why? Maybe the bug analysis is wrong. Let me think: _combine zeroes prefix when current != previous (token's label differs from label of token at chunk*K-1, i.e. the token before chunk start for chunk>0). For chunk 1 (tokens 32..63) with boundary at 40: previous = label at token 31 = 0. Tokens 32..39 have label 0 == previous → prefix applied — correct, carry scaled by alphas from chunk start, correct since same sequence. Tokens 40..63 have label 1 != 0 → prefix zeroed → no carry contribution — correct, since boundary resets. So _combine actually handles mid-chunk boundaries correctly! prefix from chunk start is exactly the product since chunk start; if a boundary occurs at token j within the chunk, tokens after j have label != label at chunk start (since labels nondecreasing) → zeroed. Correct.

_pass_states: boundary mid-chunk 1 → representative = last token label (1) != sequence (0) → factor zeroed → state = new_state (chunk summary, which itself resets intra-chunk → correct new sequence state). Correct! Labels are nondecreasing so last-token label comparison fully detects any in-chunk boundary.

So the claims are actually wrong; the design is correct. Finalize all three as rebutted.
